member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.AccountNature
member.summary: Nature of an account balance — determines whether a debit or a credit increases it. This single distinction is what makes the double-entry engine self-consistent: every posting rule reduces to "does this debit/credit increase or decrease the account's Nature".

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.AccountGroup
member.summary: Chart-of-Accounts grouping node (e.g. "Current Assets", "Operating Expenses"). Forms a self-referencing tree so the Trial Balance / Balance Sheet can be rendered hierarchically per company policy.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.Account
member.summary: Aggregate Root of the Chart of Accounts. Every financial posting in the entire ERP ultimately resolves to a debit/credit against an . The account enforces its own invariants: it cannot be posted to if it is a summary/header account (only leaf accounts accept postings), and it cannot be deactivated while it carries a non-zero balance concept is enforced at the application-service level via the ledger, not here (this aggregate only knows its own definition, not its running balance — that is a GL projection).

member.name: P:ERP.Domain.Accounting.Account.IsHeaderAccount
member.summary: Header accounts are structural only (e.g. "1000 - Assets") and cannot receive journal postings directly — only their leaf descendants can. This mirrors how SAP B1 / Dynamics BC prevent posting to summary nodes.

member.name: M:ERP.Domain.Accounting.Account.SignedEffect(System.Decimal,System.Decimal)
member.summary: Signed effect of a raw debit/credit pair on this account's natural balance. Positive result increases the account, negative decreases it. Centralizing this here means the GL balance calculator, Trial Balance, and Balance Sheet reports all derive from one authoritative rule instead of duplicating "if debit account then debit-credit else credit-debit" logic everywhere.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.CostCenter
member.summary: Cost Center — enables dimensional accounting (profit/cost tracking per department, project, or branch) orthogonal to the Chart of Accounts, as required for management reporting in any real ERP.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.FiscalYear
member.summary: Aggregate Root representing one fiscal year, composed of accounting periods (typically monthly). No journal entry may post to a period that is not Open — this is the primary control that prevents accidental/fraudulent tampering with closed books, mirroring period-lock behavior in SAP/Dynamics.

member.name: M:ERP.Domain.Accounting.FiscalYear.ClosePeriod(System.Int32,System.String)
member.summary: Closes a period after validating all prior periods are already closed — periods must close sequentially, matching real-world close procedures (cannot close March while January is still open).

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.AccountingPeriod
member.summary: Child entity of FiscalYear — the actual posting-control unit. Every JournalEntry line is validated against its period's Status before posting.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalSourceModule
member.summary: Identifies which module/document produced this entry, enabling drill-down from the General Ledger back to the originating Sales Invoice, PO, Payroll run, etc. This traceability is what separates a real accounting engine from a spreadsheet.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalEntry
member.summary:
AGGREGATE ROOT of the entire Financial Accounting module and, transitively, of the whole ERP's financial integrity. Every economic event in every other module (Sales, Purchasing, Inventory, Payroll, Fixed Assets) ultimately materializes as one JournalEntry here.
CORE INVARIANT (enforced, never bypassable): total debits MUST equal total credits at all times a JournalEntry transitions to Posted. This is not a validation rule bolted on in the Application layer — it is a domain invariant enforced inside the aggregate itself, because allowing an unbalanced entry to ever reach the database would corrupt the ledger irrecoverably.

member.name: M:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalEntry.CreateDraft(System.String,System.DateTime,System.Guid,System.Guid,System.Guid,System.Guid,System.String,ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalSourceModule,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Guid})
member.summary: Factory method — the ONLY way to construct a JournalEntry. Starts in Draft with no lines; lines are added via , and the entry can only transition to Posted through , which re-validates balance. This funnel prevents any code path from producing a malformed entry.

member.name: M:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalEntry.AddLine(System.Guid,System.Decimal,System.Decimal,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Guid},System.String)
member.summary: Adds one debit-or-credit line. A line must be exactly one-sided — a real accounting system never allows a single line to carry both a debit and a credit amount simultaneously.

member.name: M:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalEntry.Post(ERP.Domain.Accounting.AccountingPeriod)
member.summary: Posts the entry: validates the double-entry invariant, the period is open, and every referenced account is a valid leaf/postable account (that last check happens in the domain service which has access to the Account repository — this aggregate alone cannot see other aggregates, per DDD aggregate-boundary rules). On success, raises so the GL projection / read model can update asynchronously.

member.name: M:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalEntry.CreateReversal(System.String,System.DateTime,System.Guid,System.String)
member.summary: Creates a fully mirrored reversing entry (debits become credits and vice versa) for the given date. Used for period-end accruals, error correction, or cancelling a posted source document (e.g. a cancelled Sales Invoice) — never delete a posted entry; always reverse it, preserving the audit trail.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.JournalLine
member.summary: Child entity of JournalEntry (not an aggregate root — never accessed outside its parent JournalEntry). Represents a single debit or credit line.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.Services.IAccountRepository
member.summary: Repository contract for the Account aggregate (implemented in Persistence).

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.Services.JournalPostingService
member.summary:
Domain Service (per DDD: operations that don't naturally belong to a single aggregate because they coordinate several — here, JournalEntry + Account + FiscalYear). This is the single choke point every other module's posting logic (Sales, Purchasing, Payroll, Inventory, Fixed Assets) calls through, which is what guarantees the whole ERP's ledger stays internally consistent: no module is allowed to write a JournalEntry any other way.
Uses the STRATEGY pattern via — each source module supplies its own rule object describing which accounts to debit/credit for its document type (e.g. SalesInvoicePostingRule, PurchaseInvoicePostingRule, PayrollPostingRule), while this service owns the invariant enforcement (balance, period-open, account-postable) that is common to all of them.

Builds, validates, and posts a journal entry from a set of posting lines supplied by any module. This is the method a Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payroll run, or Depreciation job ultimately calls.

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Accounting.Services.IPostingRule`1
member.summary: Strategy contract implemented once per source-document type. Each module (Sales, Purchasing, Payroll...) implements this to declare "given this document, which accounts get debited/credited and by how much" without knowing anything about period control, balance validation, or persistence — that's the JournalPostingService's job. This is the Strategy pattern applied to the classic ERP problem of "every document type has different posting rules."

member.name: T:ERP.Domain.Common.Money
member.summary: Represents a monetary amount tied to a specific currency. Never use decimal/float directly for money in the domain — this VO prevents accidental cross-currency arithmetic (e.g. adding SAR to USD without conversion) at compile/run time and centralizes rounding rules (banker's rounding to the currency's minor unit).
